newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Q4 growth slowdown seen as old news.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Q4 growth slowdown seen as old news.

text.p: Australian markets received confirmation on Wednesday that the pace of economic growth has been sluggish since the middle of last year, but their focus remained more on the improving growth prospects for 1997.
Gross domestic product (GDP) rose 0.5 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, broadly in line with expectations, to be 3.1 percent higher over the course of 1996, official figures showed.
Apart from the moderate rise in the December figures, some earlier quarters were revised with the net outcome being a better reflection of the 1996 growth profile, economists said.
GDP in the September 1996 quarter rose 0.6 percent and the June quarter was up 0.3 percent, seeing the pace of annual growth slow markedly from the 5.0 percent posted in March 1996.

"What you have is the year-to number is now 3.1 percent, with three very subdued quarters...broadly consistent with the general tone of the economy through that period," Rothschild Australia chief economist Ric Simes said.
Of the three GDP measures used to derive the average figure, income based GDP (GDP-I) was the strongest, rising 0.8 percent in the quarter after some growth in company profits and wages.
Production based GDP (GDP-P) rose 0.6 percent, while the expenditure based GDP (GDP-E) was flat.
Private consumption was up 0.5 percent in the quarter, stronger than many had expected after the release in February of negative retail trade figures for the quarter.
"The most striking thing for us was that private consumption spending was a great deal stronger than people has expected," Macquarie Bank senior economist John Kyriakopoulos said.
Given the weak retail data, it meant spending on services must have risen, he said. This in turn meant the base for consumer spending into 1997 was probably better than expected.
